metas.name: Argentina - Argentina
metas.note: Phone Codes in Argentina are 10 digits, with the 3 ou 4 firsts digit wich are regionals (2 for Buenos Aires).
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Australia - Australia
metas.note: Australian phone numbers are 8 digits with a 2-digit area code in front. Mobile phone numbers are 12 digits and start with 04. Keep in mind, not all phone numbers will include an area code in front of it.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/australia.

metas.name: Austria - Austria
metas.note: 01 (Vienna) > 07
metas.footer: From : https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telephone_numbers_in_Austria

metas.name: Brazil - Brazil
metas.note:
Area codes are common to see in Brazil. They are often notated using parentheses, or at minimum as two separate numbers. Phone numbers are sometimes without area codes, and without them will be 8 numbers long for landline and 9 for mobile.

The pattern for each of the states is very learnable and useful. The area codes are grouped by first digit, so even just learning those can already help a lot. Notably, area codes ending in 1 will always be around major cities and state capitals.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Bulgaria - Bulgaria
metas.note:
Conveniently, they are ordered by first digit, so just learning the first digit can yield high results with little effort.

Numbers between parentheses in the map are area codes from a neighbouring province that frequently spill into that one.

Codes next to a small dot represent area codes unique to the province capital.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bulgaria.

metas.name: Chile - Chile
metas.note: Chilean phone codes will sometimes have a two digit area code in front, followed by seven digits. The patterns of the codes are easily memorable. Most of the central states also have different area codes for specific provinces, which can help you make accurate guesses.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/chile.

metas.name: Croatia - Croatia
metas.note: Croatian landlines typically start with a zero followed by the area code. Zagreb : 01 South : 02X North : 05X(West) > 04X(Central) > 03X(East)
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/croatia.

metas.name: Czechia - Czechia
metas.note:
Czech phone numbers are typically made up of 9 digits, of which the first 1-3 digits are the area code. Note that if the first digit is 6 or higher, it does not indicate a specific area. They’re not very common.

NOTE: Slovak phone numbers typically begin with a 0.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/czechia.

metas.name: France - France
metas.note:
French telephone numbers are 10 digits long, with the first two pairs of digits being two separate area codes, following two patterns:

01 is in Île-de-France and 02-05 goes clockwise from the northwest.

2X is in the far north, with the numbers generally increasing anticlockwise. 9X is an exception, being found both in the far northwest and far southeast.

NOTE: Phone numbers beginning with 06-09 are not regional.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/france.

metas.name: Germany - Germany
metas.note: Phones Area Codes in germany are quite lernable. It starts with 0XXXX, 02 are in the west, 03 the east, 04 -> 07 from northwest to southwest and 08->09 in the southeast. Numbers starting by 01 are mobiles.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Ghana - Ghana
metas.note:
Format 03X XXX XXXX where the 3rd digit is regional. Numbers increase from south (0) to north (9).

Any phone numbers with other prefixes (02, 05, 08...) are even mobile numbers or from an old numbering plan which is still learnable but less logical than the current one.
metas.footer: Image from : https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telephone_numbers_in_Ghana

metas.name: Greece - Greece
metas.note:
Greek area codes will always begin with a 2, followed by 1-3 digits determining the area.

NOTE: If the third digit is 1, you will be in the largest city of the region, and if the third digit is 9, you will be in the area surrounding that city.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/greece.

metas.name: Italy - Italy
metas.note: Italian area codes follow a pattern where the first digit generally increases to the east, then south.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/italy.

metas.name: Japan - Japan
metas.note:
Area codes are commonly found throughout the country and increase to the south.

NOTE: Area codes ending with a 0 are often not regional, most notably 0120.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Mexico - Mexico
metas.note: Mexico
metas.footer: 06-08 North 03-04 (/2) 05 Mexico 02-07 Around Mexico 09 (02+07) South

metas.name: Namibia - Namibia
metas.note:
Namibia area codes will always begin with 06, followed by 1 digit determining the area.

Notably, the city of Windhoek is 061
metas.footer: Image from PlonkIt discord (Luxe)

metas.name: Netherlands - Netherlands
metas.note:
Dutch landline phone numbers start with a three- or four-digit area code. These are geographically grouped, except for the ones that start with 07, and two of the 02 codes.

NOTE: Dutch mobile phone numbers start with 06, which is a code that is not used for any of the landline area codes.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/netherlands.

metas.name: New Zealand - New Zealand
metas.note: New Zealand phone numbers are seven digits with a two-digit area code in front of it. Numbers starting with 02 are mobile numbers.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: Panama - Panama
metas.note:
The first digit of phone numbers can be used to regionguess Panama.

The numbers with a smaller font indicate potentially useful regional two-digit codes.

NOTE: Only phone numbers with 7 digits are helpful, and any numbers starting with 5, 6, or 8 are useless as well.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/panama.

metas.name: Poland - Poland
metas.note:
Polish landline phone numbers have 9 digits. The first 2 digits are the area code. These area codes are distributed in a sensible manner across the country. Even just learning the first digit of the area codes can greatly narrow down the region.

NOTE: Mobile numbers also have 9 digits, but luckily there is no overlap between the first two digits of mobile numbers and landlines.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/poland.

metas.name: Portugal - Portugal
metas.note: The first three digits of Portuguese landlines make up the area codes, which are distributed as seen on the map. Phone codes not starting with a 2 are not regional, and codes starting with 29 will either be the Azores or Madeira. Lisbon is 21 and Porto is 22.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/portugal.

metas.name: Russia - Russia
metas.note: Notably, area codes starting with 8 are in the west, codes starting with 3 are fairly central and codes starting with 4 are either east (41X-42X) or around Moscow (47X-48X-49X).
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Slovakia - Slovakia
metas.note:
Slovak phone numbers typically consist of 10 digits, of which the first 2-3 digits are the area code.

NOTE: Czech phone numbers generally do not begin with a 0.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/slovakia.

metas.name: South Africa - South Africa
metas.note:
Telephone numbers are 10 digits long. The first three digits of landline numbers are the area code. The first digit is always a zero; the second and third digits give you the area. The area codes are geographically grouped, so even learning just the first digit is useful.

NOTE: Mobile phone numbers start with 06–08. These numbers are not specific to an area.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/south-africa.

metas.name: South Korea - South Korea
metas.note: Area codes in South Korea increase to the south, from 02 in the north, to 064 on Jeju. It is also notable that Seoul has the only two-digit area code in the country.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/south-korea.

metas.name: Spain - Spain
metas.note:
Area codes in Spain are very useful, as you only need two digits to get a very accurate guess. Every landline number starts with “9”, followed by the regional numbers.

Mobile numbers start with “6”, and are not relevant in region guessing.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/spain.

metas.name: Sri Lanka - Sri Lanka
metas.note:
Sri Lankan telephone numbers have 10 digits.

The first three digits of landline phone numbers are the area code. The first digit of that area code is always a 0, while the remaining two digits are shown on the map.

Mobile phone numbers always start with 07 and are not associated with any particular region.

Image credit: Maccem.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sri-lanka.

metas.name: Sweden - Sweden
metas.note:
The first 3-4 (2 in Stockholm) digits of landline phone numbers in Sweden are the area code. The map shows the first two digits in every region. Within the regions, the third and fourth digit of area codes typically increase to the northeast.

NOTE: Mobile phone numbers always begin with 07.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: Taiwan - Taiwan
metas.note:
Taiwan telephone numbers are 10 digits, with the first two digits indicating the area code. Area codes range from 02 to 08, increasing as you go south.

NOTE: Oftentimes the area code will be written within parentheses. Mobile numbers start with 09.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/taiwan.

metas.name: Thailand - Thailand
metas.note:
Thai landline phone numbers have 9 digits. The first digits of phone numbers are the area code. The Bangkok area code is 02, the other area codes have three digits. The area codes are grouped, so even just learning the first digit is useful.

NOTE: Mobile phone numbers start with 08 or 09 and have 10 digits. None of these numbers overlap with the area codes. Numbers starting with 06 are also not regional.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Turkey - Turkey
metas.note:
Turkish area codes follow a fairly easy to learn pattern and can be very useful to get the general region. Most notably, the first digit of area codes are ordered from 2 in the west to 4 in the east.

NOTE: Phone codes starting with 5 are not regional.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/turkey.

metas.name: Vietnam - Vietnam
metas.note: In Vietnam, phone numbers start with 0, if it starts with 02 it's a regional number with 2X or 2XX defining an area. Numbers are fairly easy to learn, with 24 for Hanoi, 28 for Ho Chi Minh City, area codes increase from north (2OX) to south (29X).
